_comment: Pre-registered council ATTENDANCE metrics (road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-b Phase 1.4). Registered here rather than in roadmap prose because a roadmap is archived when it closes and a metric outlives it — the sibling budget files (hook-token-budget.json, recycle-threshold-budget.json) already carry the owner / review_by / honest-gap discipline this reuses. The instrument is the quorum_result line appendQuorumEvent writes to agents/runtime/council/events.log (schema v5 since road-to-council-evidence-integrity Phase 3 added stance_agreement, on top of the ADR-224 shadow floor which added gate_class + floor_would_hold at v3 and min_present at v4; v2 lines carry none of the three, v3 lines carry no min_present, and v4-and-earlier lines carry no stance_agreement, so a rate over them must exclude rather than assume them); nothing here is measured yet, and no threshold is committed before data exists.
privacy: a quorum_result line carries {phase, command, dispatch, verdict, threshold, configured_total, total, present, solo, gate_class, min_present, floor_would_hold, absent[{member, reason}]} — counts, closed vocabularies, booleans, and member ids only. The type has no field able to hold free-form content, so the CLI's own `detail` string (provider error text, which can embed paths and prompt fragments) is dropped at the boundary rather than scrubbed. The two v3 additions are booleans, the v4 addition is a small integer read from config, and the v5 addition is a three-value closed vocabulary (consensus | split | not_tallied) derived from tally_stances — none of which can widen that surface. stance_agreement in particular carries no option LABEL: the labels members vote on are free-form member text, so recording which option won would have opened exactly the free-form hole the type is built to refuse.
phase_split: A pass emits `pre_run` (build_members — who could be constructed) and, on the `run` path, `post_run` (_postRunQuorum — who actually returned a usable response). They disagree whenever a member constructs and then fails mid-flight, so a rate computed over both double-counts. A `pre_run` line is NOT evidence a pass ran: `command: estimate` is a spend-free preview, and a `run` / `debate` line is written before the `--confirm` gate (which defaults to false and returns before any provider call) and before the necessity and size-fit gates. A `post_run` line is the only line that proves providers were called — which is why every rate below is post_run-scoped, and why `command` exists at all.

attendance_rate.definition: of the members that entered the pass, how many answered: present / total per post_run pass. Bounded by 1 by construction (evaluateQuorum clamps present into [0, total]).
attendance_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, fields present + total
attendance_rate.threshold: none committed before data — baseline first, threshold at review date

roster_shortfall_rate.definition: how often the council shrank BEFORE the pass: share of post_run passes with total < configured_total, plus the size of the gap. This is the half attendance_rate cannot see — a pass with 3 configured, 2 failing to construct and 1 answering reads 1/1 = 100 % attendance and a shortfall of 2. Both numbers are needed and neither substitutes for the other; a single ratio over mixed rosters is the error this pair replaces.
roster_shortfall_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, configured_total vs total
roster_shortfall_rate.threshold: none committed before data — baseline first, threshold at review date
roster_shortfall_rate.not_an_error: total > configured_total is legitimate and not a shortfall: `--siblings` fans ONE enabled config entry into N clients, so the client roster can exceed the entry count. configured_total counts enabled config ENTRIES; total counts CLIENTS. Compare them for direction, never divide one by the other.

solo_conclusion_rate.definition: share of post_run passes with `solo: true` — written by the isSoloConcluded predicate in quorum.ts, never re-derived from the numbers here, so one change to the rule cannot leave this definition stale. ceil(n/2) makes 1-of-2 a legitimate conclusion; this measures how often that legitimacy is used, not whether it should be. THREE cases carry solo: true and they are not the same finding — a degraded multi-member council (configured_total > 1), a council configured with one member (configured_total = 1, dispatch = full), and a deliberate --single dispatch (dispatch = single). Split on dispatch and configured_total before reading the rate.
solo_conclusion_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, field solo, split by dispatch + configured_total
solo_conclusion_rate.threshold: DECIDED 2026-08-11 against real data — see ADR-224 (docs/decisions/ADR-224-gate-scoped-solo-attendance-floor.md). The quorum-solo-floor blocker pre-registered three outcomes — a third CLI member, a gate-scoped min_present: 2, or a published null under 5 %. Read at 2026-08-11T09:30Z with the definition above: 1 of 8 post_run/command=run passes carried a degraded solo conclusion = 12.5 %, so the under-5 % null did not fire and the gate-scoped floor was chosen (council 2/2). It was decided on the degraded case only; a --single pass is the operator asking for one voice, not the council failing to assemble. Still no numeric threshold is committed here, deliberately: at n=8 the 95 % interval around 1/8 spans roughly 0.3 %-53 %, so the rate established urgency and not certainty, and ADR-224's review trigger reopens the null at n=40. What this metric measures does NOT change; once the floor lands, how often it FIRES is a second and different question needing its own instrument.

shadow_floor_fire_rate.definition: share of post_run passes where a min_present floor WOULD have held the pass, had one been enforced: `floor_would_hold: true` over post_run/command=run lines. Written by the wouldSoloFloorHold predicate in quorum.ts, never re-derived from present/threshold here, for the same reason solo_conclusion_rate defers to isSoloConcluded — one definition, so a change to the rule cannot leave this file stale. This is the instrument solo_conclusion_rate's threshold note said the FIRING question would need; it answers 'how often would the floor hold a gate', which is NOT the question solo_conclusion_rate answers ('how often did a pass conclude on one voice'). The two are NOT the same rate and diverge in both directions. solo: true / floor_would_hold: false — a council configured with one member (the ceiling clamps to 1, deliberately). solo: false / floor_would_hold: true — any pass concluding on 2+ voices under a configured quorum_min_present above 2. They also AGREE on the case that matters most: a construction-degraded roster (2 configured, 1 constructed, 1 answered) is solo: true and floor_would_hold: true, because the floor is judged against max(total, configured_total) — judging it against total alone made this pass, the very one ADR-224 was decided on, structurally unable to fire.
shadow_floor_fire_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, field floor_would_hold, split by dispatch + configured_total AND BY min_present (schema v4+)
shadow_floor_fire_rate.threshold: none committed before data — and deliberately none at the review date either unless a gate-class caller exists by then. A fire-rate over passes that gate nothing measures a counterfactual, not a risk; it is registered now so ADR-224's review trigger (b) has an accumulating series rather than a series that starts on the day someone remembers to add one.
shadow_floor_fire_rate.split_by_min_present_or_the_rate_is_unin: The floor this rate counts against is `quorum_min_present`, which lives in the USER-GLOBAL .ai-council.yml (ADR-104) — per developer machine, gitignored, invisible in this repository. Schema v3 consumed that value and did not record it, so two operators produced byte-identical lines while measuring different counterfactuals, and a pooled rate over them was a mean of incomparable things. Schema v4 records it as `min_present`; group on it before reading, and treat v3 lines as a separate stratum whose floor is UNKNOWN rather than assuming the default. The sharpest case: `quorum_min_present: 1` is valid config and, per the predicate's own test, can never hold anything — so it drives this rate to a permanent zero. Without min_present on the line that zero is indistinguishable from 'the floor genuinely never would have fired', which is precisely the reading ADR-224's review trigger (b) would act on. No threshold was loosened by adding this field; nothing was gated on it before.
shadow_floor_fire_rate.nothing_is_enforced: No value of this metric holds, delays or fails a council pass. wouldSoloFloorHold is a counterfactual with no caller branching on it, and quorum_min_present configures only what the counterfactual is computed against. A reader must not cite this rate as evidence that the floor protected anything — it has never protected anything.

absent_reason_distribution.definition: count per reason over absent[] entries — no_binary / no_auth / timeout / quota (AbsentReason) plus the two runtime fallbacks the CLI writes directly, `unavailable` (transport resolved to nothing) and `binary_missing` (a CLI client refused to construct). Distinguishes a council degraded by configuration from one degraded by provider behaviour, which have opposite fixes.
absent_reason_distribution.instrument: quorum_result lines, absent[].reason, split by phase (a pre_run absence is configuration; a post_run absence is mid-flight). Excluding `command: estimate` is NOT sufficient: `run` and `debate` also reach construction and return at the `--confirm` gate, which defaults to false. The reliable filter is a pre_run line whose pass produced a matching post_run line; a pre_run line with no post_run partner reached construction and stopped there, whatever its command says.
absent_reason_distribution.threshold: none committed before data — the distribution IS the finding at review date
absent_reason_distribution.merge_before_reading: `no_binary` and `binary_missing` are two spellings of one condition — the CLI binary is unusable — written by different code paths (transport_resolver's static classification vs the CLI client's construction failure). They are recorded separately because that is what the tree emits, not because they are separate findings; merge them before reading the distribution, or the largest bucket is split in two.

honest_null_consequence: If the log accumulates and the solo-conclusion rate sits near zero, that is the published answer to the quorum-solo-floor blocker and 1.5 is cancelled against it — not quietly dropped. If attendance data never accumulates at all (nobody runs a metered council pass in the window), that is reported as an unmeasured metric at the review date, never as a passing one.
honest_gaps: `lens` and `invocation` are empty on every pre_run line — neither is known at member-construction time — so any per-lens breakdown is post_run-only.

`command: debate` carries the pre_run half ONLY. There is no _postRunQuorum on the debate path, and defining `usable response` for a multi-round debate is a separate question this registration does not answer. So debate contributes to absent_reason_distribution and to nothing else: attendance_rate and solo_conclusion_rate cover the `run` path, and a reader must not read them as covering every metered pass.

A pre_run line proves construction happened, never that a pass followed — the `--confirm` gate (default false), the necessity gate and the size-fit gate all abort afterwards and nothing on the line records it. Any count over pre_run lines is an upper bound; pair it with a post_run line before treating it as a pass.

`gate_class` is `false` on EVERY line written so far and will stay false until a caller declares otherwise — nothing in the tree branches on QuorumStatus to hold a gate, so there is no gate-class caller to mark. shadow_floor_fire_rate is therefore a rate over ALL post_run passes, not over gate-class ones, and the gate-class-scoped rate ADR-224 actually cares about is UNMEASURED, not zero. Do not read a `false` majority as evidence that gate-class passes are rare; it is evidence that the concept has no consumer yet.

The CLI emit wiring itself has no test. The two modules are covered directly, but nothing exercises build_members / cmd_run / cmd_debate end-to-end against a captured log — and `_emitQuorumEvent` forwards no AppendEventOptions, so there is no target to capture into. Two defects in this file's first version (a `dispatch` written from the flag rather than the outcome, and a rate mixing config entries with clients) were found by review rather than by a test, which is what that gap costs.

stance_agreement measures agreement among the members that ANSWERED and were parseable — it says nothing about a member that was absent or unparsed, which the attendance fields on the same line cover separately. A pass reading `1/2 present · stance_agreement: consensus` is one voice agreeing with itself, and the two fields must be read together; neither is a summary of the other.

stance_agreement_rate.definition: share of passes whose seats reached consensus: `stance_agreement: 'consensus'` over post_run/command=run lines AT SCHEMA >= 5. Three values, not a boolean, and the third is why this metric can exist honestly: stance tallying is opt-in and off by default, so most passes never ask the question — `not_tallied` records that, where a boolean would have been forced to write `false` and read as disagreement. Written by tally_stances' own verdict (`consensus !== null` vs `split`), never re-derived from the tally numbers here, the same one-definition discipline solo_conclusion_rate follows by deferring to isSoloConcluded.
stance_agreement_rate.instrument: quorum_result lines, phase=post_run, command=run, field stance_agreement — replayed by `./scripts-run src/scripts/council_attendance_metrics`, which prints this rate next to its denominator and its excluded count
stance_agreement_rate.threshold: none committed before data — baseline first, threshold at review date. Nothing is gated on this value and no pass is held, delayed or failed by it.
stance_agreement_rate.exclude_pre_v5_lines_or_the_rate_is_inve: A v4-and-earlier line carries no stance_agreement field and NO honest value can be inferred for it: that pass may have run a tally whose verdict was never recorded, or none at all, and the line cannot tell you which. So the denominator is v5+ lines only. Defaulting the missing field to `not_tallied` manufactures a measurement out of an absence — on the committed span fixture it moves the rate from 1/3 to 1/6, a plausible number with nothing behind it. `attendance_metrics.test.ts` asserts both the exclusion and its mirror (dropping the v4 stratum must not move the rate), and the sabotage that defaults instead of excluding fails both.
stance_agreement_rate.denominator_is_not_the_attendance_denomi: agreement_eligible is a SUBSET of passes, so this rate and the four above are computed over different populations and must never be presented as parts of one table without their own denominators printed. The replay prints both counts on the line for exactly that reason.
